status: frozen after the thermal-source protocol and before any regional temperature result, thermal source map, v17 inverse coefficient, or v17 lensing score existed
pre_target_halo_scale_addition: Before either spent lensing target was opened, v1.0.1 added an amplitude-independent one-metric residual-field extent diagnostic. It measures whether the baryon-derived thermal response predicts the target residual's R50 and R80 field-energy radii after the unchanged transferred static baseline. No target value, fitted coefficient, feature, smoothing scale, ridge alpha, or existing gate was read or changed.
purpose: Test whether independently measured projected gas thermal stress adds transferable spatial information to the unchanged v16B internal-baryon baseline on the two spent clusters.

authorization.prohibition: Do not import, construct, or evaluate either spent lensing target until the thermal-source report and both source-product hashes exist and pass validation.

sample.target_interpretation: same-catalog conventional halo reconstruction used only as a spent inverse target, not raw truth or a holdout

static_baseline.feature_family: the unchanged five-scale v16B internal-only one-metric family
static_baseline.rule: Fit the internal coefficients on the training cluster, transfer them unchanged to the other cluster, and freeze that prediction before fitting any thermal increment.

thermal_features.one_metric_rule: Every scalar source and scale supplies one convergence/shear_1/shear_2 triplet, and exactly one real coefficient multiplies all three channels.

fit.selection: minimum symmetric leave-one-cluster-out full-field NRMSE on the spent pair

resolution_control.change_metric: maximum of relative change in symmetric and directional full-field NRMSE, absolute change in directional residual-shear alignment and residual-power closure, and relative change in transferred thermal R50 and R80 field-energy radii

halo_scale_diagnostic.scientific_question: Does the spatial extent of the baryon-derived response predict the apparent halo-like residual extent without fitting a cluster radius?
halo_scale_diagnostic.required_field: remaining target one-metric triplet after the unchanged static coefficients trained on the opposite cluster
halo_scale_diagnostic.predicted_field: thermal one-metric triplet using the same coefficients trained on the opposite cluster
halo_scale_diagnostic.center_definition: the field-energy centroid is computed independently for the required and predicted triplets so extent is not confused with centroid offset; full-field NRMSE and shear alignment continue to score position
halo_scale_diagnostic.radius_definition: R_p is the smallest centroided radius enclosing fraction p of summed field energy
halo_scale_diagnostic.amplitude_invariance: multiplying every channel by one nonzero scalar leaves R50 and R80 unchanged
halo_scale_diagnostic.zero_or_nonfinite_field_rule: the scale gate fails; no radius is imputed
halo_scale_diagnostic.claim_boundary: This is a model-derived residual-field extent diagnostic on two spent clusters, not a measured dark-halo radius and not observational validation.

decision_rule: Advance only if the static baseline is reproduced, the zero-thermal limit is valid, and every improvement, absolute-error, alignment, power, halo-scale, and resolution gate passes simultaneously.
If stage A passes, the next task is to derive the response from one universally coupled healthy action; no inverse coefficient may be promoted to a gravity constant.

If stage A fails, reject the tested resolved projected gas thermal-stress source at this resolution and do not rescue it with a cluster label, private normalization, fitted orientation, or lens-only law.
A stage-A failure does not reject collisionless member stress, causal history, line-of-sight structure, or a materially different carrier.
No outcome on this spent pair validates a theory or authorizes opening an untouched cluster.
claim_boundary: This is a source-information diagnostic on two spent, model-derived comparator maps, not a gravity theory and not an observational validation.
The thermal proxy is constructed from independent baryonic X-ray measurements before the spent target is opened.
The compared thermal families are predeclared nested hypotheses, not a formula selected from an object label.

A transferable inverse pattern would still have to emerge from one action governing both massive matter and photons, pass galaxy and raw multi-cluster lensing holdouts, and satisfy Solar-System and stability constraints.
